latest_apis.rationale: The stack is consistently the current generation — v22's @Service, stable resource(), signal inputs, native control flow, zoneless — with only two documented deviations (effect-as-state-sync, ignored abortSignal) and hand-rolled scroll logic the router can supply.

evidence: app/src/app/core/poke-api.ts — single data-access module (fetch, cache, 404-as-domain-error) behind typed models in core/models.ts
app/src/app/core/api-config.ts:9-16 — API origin read from a meta tag via InjectionToken factory, so one build works against any API without rebuilds

churn_resistance.rationale: Upgrading Angular or changing the API surface would touch few files (one service, view-model builders, pure tested helpers), and config is centralized; the scattered hand-rolled scroll logic and selector-coupled global CSS are the main places future churn will land.

findings.issue: effect() is used to copy the q route input into the searchText signal with a manual lastSearchSent escape hatch — the state-sync anti-pattern the framework docs call out ('Never use an effect to sync one piece of state to another').
findings.suggestion: Model searchText as linkedSignal({source: this.q, computation: v => v ?? ''}) (v22 core API) so URL changes reset the editable value without the effect/flag bookkeeping.

findings.issue: No resource loader passes its abortSignal to fetch, so superseded loads (e.g. navigating between Pokémon) cannot be cancelled; docs mandate 'Always pass abortSignal to your fetch calls'.
findings.suggestion: Thread the loader's abortSignal through PokeApi.get (e.g. an options arg) into fetch(url, {signal}), keeping the in-flight cache but evicting aborted entries on AbortError.

findings.issue: Scroll management is hand-rolled in three separate places (app.ts path-change, home.ts pagination, pokemon-page.ts #moves fragment), duplicating behavior the router provides and fragment behavior the browser provides.
findings.suggestion: Use provideRouter(routes, withComponentInputBinding(), withInMemoryScrolling({scrollPositionRestoration: 'top', anchorScrolling: 'enabled'})) and keep only the post-data #moves scroll as custom logic.

findings.issue: effect() + afterNextRender(..., {injector}) re-implements post-render DOM work; afterRenderEffect is the current API for reading/writing the DOM after render, and the explicit injector is noise since the effect already runs in an injection context.
findings.suggestion: Replace the effect/afterNextRender combo with afterRenderEffect(...) (or move the fragment scroll into an afterRenderEffect that reads moves.hasValue()).

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but is never imported; the app deliberately uses native controls plus URL-bound state, so the package is dead weight in the install tree.

All styles are global and several rules target component tag selectors (app-load-state, .site-main > app-home, router-outlet), so renaming or restructuring components requires synchronized CSS edits and the styles live far from their components.
findings.suggestion: Move page/component-specific rules into per-component styles (Angular's default emulated encapsulation) and keep only genuinely shared tokens/base styles in styles.css.

findings.issue: spriteUrl hardcodes the media path pattern (/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png) instead of deriving sprite URLs from API payloads, coupling the card grid to an external convention the API could change.
findings.suggestion: Where payload sprite URLs exist use them (as pokemon-data.ts:56 already does for artwork); for card lists, consider a single documented constant next to the API base configuration so the assumption is visible in one place.

findings.issue: prettier is installed as a devDependency with a .prettierrc but no npm script runs it, so formatting is not reproducible from the repo alone.
findings.suggestion: Add a "format" script (prettier --write .) or drop the dependency.

summary: This is an aggressively current Angular 22 codebase — @Service, stable resource(), signal inputs, native control flow, zoneless, Vitest — with a lean dependency set and a clean single-module data layer that will absorb framework and API changes with few edits. The forward-looking deductions are concentrated in three places: an effect used as state sync where linkedSignal is the documented primitive, resource loaders that ignore abortSignal, and scroll behavior hand-rolled in three components instead of the router's built-in features. Fixing those would make it a reference-quality example.

apis.replacement: — (introduced in v22 as the successor to Injectable({providedIn:'root'}))
— (stabilized in v22; loaders should honor abortSignal)
linkedSignal({source}) for user-editable state that resets with its source
afterRenderEffect() is the current API for post-render DOM reads/writes
— (still the recommended way to render a template repeatedly, per queries-and-projection.md)
